question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?
explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and leftover electrolytes from food waste to form solid feces before elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h1)

question: A patient has a hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum (impaction), yet they keep passing small amounts of liquid. Why does this happen?

options.A: Infection has completely liquefied the entire colon
options.B: Liquid stool leaks around the solid blocked mass
options.C: The small intestine is hyperactive and rushing food
options.D: The kidneys are producing excessive fluid waste

explanation: Don't let this trick you in the ward! Liquid waste from higher up in the gut finds a way to slip past the hard, blocked stool, which can easily look like normal diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which medication class is well-known for causing severe constipation as a side effect?
explanation: Opioids slow down the movement of the gastrointestinal tract significantly, leading to hard, difficult-to-pass stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h2)

question: Between these patients, who is most at risk of developing constipation from slowed body movement?

options.A: A nursing student drinking several cups of coffee daily
options.B: A young athlete who drinks water after a football match
options.C: An older adult on strict bed rest after hip surgery
options.D: A patient with a mild viral stomach flu and loose stools

explanation: Well done! Staying in bed without moving, especially as we grow older, slows down natural bowel activity and makes constipation a major risk. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h2)

question: When assessing the tummy (abdomen), why must a nurse listen with a stethoscope *before* pressing or feeling around?

options.A: Hospital policy strictly requires listening before touching
options.B: Palpation can alter bowel sounds and mislead the exam
options.C: Auscultation warms up the stethoscope for the patient
options.D: Palpation causes immediate severe pain in all patients

explanation: Think of it this way: if you press on the tummy first, you wake up the intestines and change the sounds! Always listen before you touch. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h3)

question: How long must you listen with a stethoscope in a single part of the tummy before you can safely write down that there are 'no bowel sounds'?
explanation: It takes patience! Bowel sounds can sometimes be very quiet and lazy, so you must listen for a full five minutes in each area before deciding they are truly gone. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is a major safety worry when a nurse has to manually remove a hard stool impaction with gloved fingers?

options.A: Immediate development of permanent bowel incontinence
options.B: Sudden severe spikes in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve causing bradycardia
options.D: Accidental puncture of the abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Be careful here! Messing around in the rectum can trigger the vagus nerve, causing a sudden drop in heart rate. Always keep an eye on your patient's pulse. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which type of laxative works primarily by drawing water into the stool through osmosis?
explanation: Osmotic laxatives hold water inside the intestine, which softens hard stools and encourages bowel movements. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs sometimes avoided when a patient has an infection causing their diarrhea?

options.A: Diarrhea helps the kidneys filter extra salt from the blood
options.B: Antibiotics are the only approved treatment for any diarrhea
options.C: These medications always cause permanent bowel paralysis instantly
options.D: Stopping stool too fast can trap harmful bacteria inside the body

explanation: Makes sense, right? Diarrhea is actually the body's way of flushing out bad germs. Shutting it down too quickly can trap those toxins inside. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h5)

question: A patient with terrible watery diarrhea has raw, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing care?

options.A: Apply a drying powder to absorb moisture and stop wiping
options.B: Scrub the irritated skin firmly with soap and a rough cloth
options.C: Leave the skin exposed to room air without any protection
options.D: Clean the area gently, dry it, and apply a barrier cream

explanation: You got it! Liquid stool is harsh on the skin. Clean gently and use a good barrier cream to protect raw areas from irritation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h5)

question: What happens if a patient starts eating a lot of fiber but forgets to drink enough water?

options.A: The patient will immediately develop severe watery diarrhea
options.B: Constipation can actually worsen because stool becomes dry and bulky
options.C: Kidney function will fail due to excess nutrient absorption
options.D: Fiber will pass through the body completely unchanged

explanation: Remember: fiber acts like a sponge! Without water, it cannot swell properly and will just form a hard, difficult lump in the gut. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which food group is the best natural source of dietary fiber to promote healthy bowel movements?

options.A: Fatty red meats and processed dairy products
options.B: Processed white bread and refined white rice
options.C: Fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
options.D: Clear sugary beverages and bottled juices

explanation: Plant-based foods and whole grains contain high amounts of natural fiber, which bulks stool and stimulates regular elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h6)
